title: Range-wide sampling and genomic analyses delimit entities within the morphologically challenging Grevillea brachystylis complex
content:
Abstract
Species complexes are challenging to disentangle because the typical morphological, ecological, and life history traits used as markers of speciation are not obvious. Yet, it is these morphologically challenging complexes for which accurate taxonomy remains most critical. This is primarily because identifying taxonomic units provides identifiable targets on which conservation efforts can be focused. In the present study, we use range-wide sampling and genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphisms to assess species boundaries within the Grevillea brachystylis complex, which currently includes several conservation-listed taxa. Our data recovered five genetic clusters across ordination, sNMF, and distance-based network analyses. Analysis of molecular variance testing for different scenarios of grouping populations into putative taxa, showed the greatest partitioning of variation among five genetic clusters, compared to models based on the existing taxonomy or combining genetic clusters. These five clusters largely aligned with four existing taxa and one informal taxon, which we recommend be formally named and described. Last, we assessed patterns of heterozygosity and found a consistent pattern of inbreeding across all populations. By including genomic data to increase our understanding of this species complex, we provide greater confidence in the delimitation of these taxa and emphasize the importance of accurate taxonomy in helping identify, manage, and conserve threatened taxa.
